references.phrase: colimit of a diagram of sets
become equal at some later common stage
references.disposition: In a filtered diagram of sets, representatives become equivalent when their images agree after passing to a suitable common successor; this describes the defining colimit equivalence already captured by the existing set-colimit target, not a separate named prerequisite. It is not asserted for arbitrary category objects.
The eventual equality description refers to set-valued diagrams and is not an elementwise definition valid in every category C.

references.matching_note: This source phrase bundles two mathematically different prerequisite constructions; separate complete references have been recorded without equating an ideal power with the quotient ring.
references.phrase: quotient ring R/I^n and ideal powers

references.disposition: The canonical ring map sends r to its compatible residue-class tuple (r mod I^n)_n; it is induced by the quotient maps and inverse-limit cone already explicitly involved in the I-adic completion definition. It need not be injective without separatedness, and the map is not a new independent prerequisite meaning.
The inverse system uses the natural transition maps between ideal-power quotients and not arbitrary unrelated quotient rings.

references.context: Commutative algebra: quotient ring A/I of a commutative unital ring A by an ideal I, with elements additive cosets a+I, operations induced from A and canonical surjective unital quotient map A→A/I. This includes prime-ideal quotients, polynomial-ring quotients and ideal-power quotients; a quotient's being a field, local ring or R-algebra requires additional conditions.
references.matching_note: Ordinary quotient ring by the nth power ideal; ideal-power construction is separately recorded.

references.context: Commutative algebra: product IJ of two ideals of a commutative unital ring R, generated by finite sums of pairwise products; ordinary ideal powers I^n for n≥1 by repeated ideal multiplication, and by convention I^0=R when nonnegative exponents are used.
references.matching_note: The ideal power itself is formed by repeated ideal multiplication, independently of the quotient ring R/I^n.
